messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Let's add a new feature—bots. Bots can be members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API.

Any chat member can create and manage bots via the user interface:
- open the account settings page (`/account/edit`)
- click the bot icon ("Set up chat bots")

This opens the bots page (`/bots`). It lists the bots you created (administrators see all bots) and has the "Add a chat bot" button. The button opens the `/bots/new` page with a form:

- bot avatar (optional)
- bot name (required), labelled "Name the bot"
- the "Save changes" button

Submitting the form creates a bot and redirects back to `/bots`. Each bot on the list shows its name and its unique bot code in a read-only field labelled "Bot code", in the same list item—the code is used to authenticate bot requests. The bot code is a sensitive credential. The bots page shows all of your bots on one page, without pagination.

From the list, you can also edit a bot (name, avatar): each bot has an "Edit <bot name>" link (for example, "Edit Deploy Bot") to its edit page. The edit page uses the same form and has a "Delete this chat bot" button that asks for confirmation. A deleted bot can no longer post messages.

Like any new user, a new bot joins all open rooms. Bots can be added to other rooms the same way as people.

Here is how a bot can post a message:

```
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

Bots can post from shell scripts and CI jobs. The raw request body becomes the message body. No JSON envelope, no field names.

The endpoint responds with:

- `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`
- `422 Unprocessable Content` — empty body and no attachment
- `404 Not Found` — bad room id
- `401 Unauthorized` — invalid bot code

The message is broadcast to connected clients and triggers push notifications exactly as a human-authored message would.

The message shows the bot (its name) as the author.

# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

## Development

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
Please see our [development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Campfire set up for local development.

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability and a description of our trust model.
# How to contribute to Campfire

Campfire uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open
issues all represent agreed-upon tasks that are either being worked on, or are
ready to be worked on.

This should also make it easier to see what's in progress, and to find
something to work on if you'd like to do so.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are
   grateful for the help!
2. You'll want to make sure someone else isn't already working on the same
   issue. If they are, it will be tagged "in progress" and/or it should be clear
   from the comments. When in doubt, you can always comment on the issue to ask.
3. Similarly, if you need any help or guidance on the issue, please comment on
   the issue as you go, and we'll do our best to help.
4. When you have something ready for review or collaboration, open a PR.

### If you've found a bug...

1. If you don't have steps to reproduce the problem, or you're not certain it's a
   bug, open a discussion.
2. If you have steps to reproduce, open an issue.

### If you have an idea for a feature...

1. Open a discussion.

### If you have a question, or are having trouble with configuration...

1. Open a discussion.

Hopefully this process makes it easier for everyone to be involved. Thanks for
helping! ❤️

Rails.application.routes.draw do
  root "welcome#show"

  resource :first_run

  resource :session do
    scope module: "sessions" do
      resources :transfers, only: %i[ show update ]
    end
  end

  resource :account do
    scope module: "accounts" do
      resources :users

      resource :join_code, only: :create
      resource :logo, only: %i[ show destroy ]
      resource :custom_styles, only: %i[ edit update ]
    end
  end

  direct :fresh_account_logo do |options|
    route_for :account_logo, v: Current.account&.updated_at&.to_fs(:number), size: options[:size]
  end

  get "join/:join_code", to: "users#new", as: :join
  post "join/:join_code", to: "users#create"

  resources :qr_code, only: :show

  resources :users, only: :show do
    scope module: "users" do
      resource :avatar, only: %i[ show destroy ]
      resource :ban, only: %i[ create destroy ]

      scope defaults: { user_id: "me" } do
        resource :sidebar, only: :show
        resource :profile
        resources :push_subscriptions do
          scope module: "push_subscriptions" do
            resources :test_notifications, only: :create
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  namespace :autocompletable do
    resources :users, only: :index
  end

  direct :fresh_user_avatar do |user, options|
    route_for :user_avatar, user.avatar_token, v: user.updated_at.to_fs(:number)
  end

  resources :rooms do
    resources :messages

    scope module: "rooms" do
      resource :refresh, only: :show
      resource :settings, only: :show
      resource :involvement, only: %i[ show update ]
    end

    get "@:message_id", to: "rooms#show", as: :at_message
  end

  namespace :rooms do
    resources :opens
    resources :closeds
    resources :directs
  end

  resources :messages do
    scope module: "messages" do
      resources :boosts
    end
  end

  resources :searches, only: %i[ index create ] do
    delete :clear, on: :collection
  end

  resource :unfurl_link, only: :create

  get "webmanifest"    => "pwa#manifest"
  get "service-worker" => "pwa#service_worker"

  get "up" => "rails/health#show", as: :rails_health_check
end
"

class Room::MessagePusher
  attr_reader :room, :message

  def initialize(room:, message:)
    @room, @message = room, message
  end

  def push
    build_payload.tap do |payload|
      push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def build_payload
      if room.direct?
        build_direct_payload
      else
        build_shared_payload
      end
    end

    def build_direct_payload
      {
        title: message.creator.name,
        body: message.plain_text_body,
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def build_shared_payload
      {
        title: room.name,
        body: "#{message.creator.name}: #{message.plain_text_body}",
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(message.mentionees)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(mentionees)
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_mentions).where(user_id: mentionees.ids)
    end

    def relevant_subscriptions
      Push::Subscription
        .joins(user: :memberships)
        .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: room).where.not(user: message.creator))
    end

    def enqueue_payload_for_delivery(payload, subscriptions)
      Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.queue(payload, subscriptions)
    end
end

class Room::MessagePusher
  attr_reader :room, :message

  def initialize(room:, message:)
    @room, @message = room, message
  end

  def push
    build_payload.tap do |payload|
      push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def build_payload
      if room.direct?
        build_direct_payload
      else
        build_shared_payload
      end
    end

    def build_direct_payload
      {
        title: message.creator.name,
        body: message.plain_text_body,
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def build_shared_payload
      {
        title: room.name,
        body: "#{message.creator.name}: #{message.plain_text_body}",
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(message.mentionees)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(mentionees)
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_mentions).where(user_id: mentionees.ids)
    end

    def relevant_subscriptions
      Push::Subscription
        .joins(user: :memberships)
        .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: room).where.not(user: message.creator))
    end

    def enqueue_payload_for_delivery(payload, subscriptions)
      Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.queue(payload, subscriptions)
    end
end

  end

    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type

        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end

      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)

      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include SessionLookup

  included do
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :signed_in?

    protect_from_forgery with: :exception
  end

  class_methods do
    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
    end

    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :restore_authentication, :redirect_signed_in_user_to_root, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_in?
      Current.user.present?
    end

    def require_authentication
      restore_authentication || request_authentication
    end

    def restore_authentication
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        resume_session session
      end
    end

    def request_authentication
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      redirect_to new_session_url
    end

    def redirect_signed_in_user_to_root
      redirect_to root_url if signed_in?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(user)
      user.sessions.start!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        authenticated_as session
      end
    end

    def resume_session(session)
      session.resume user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip
      authenticated_as session
    end

    def terminate_current_session
      Current.session&.destroy!
      reset_session
      remove_authentication_cookie
    end

    def authenticated_as(session)
      Current.session = session
      set_authentication_cookie(session)
    end

    def post_authenticating_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || root_url
    end

    def set_authentication_cookie(session)
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def remove_authentication_cookie
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end
end

    render action: :room_not_found
  end

  def show
  end

  end

        @room.messages.with_creator.page_after(@room.messages.find(params[:after]))
      else
        @room.messages.with_creator.last_page
      end
    end

      params.require(:message).permit(:body, :attachment, :client_message_id)
    end

  DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME = "New room"

  def show
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  def new
    @room  = Rooms::Closed.new(name: DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME)
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Closed.create_for(room_params, users: grantees)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
    selected_user_ids = @room.users.pluck(:id)
    @selected_users, @unselected_users = User.active.ordered.partition { |user| selected_user_ids.include?(user.id) }
  end

  def update
    @room.update! room_params
    @room.memberships.revise(granted: grantees, revoked: revokees)

    broadcast_update_room
    redirect_to room_url(@room)

    # Allows us to edit an open room and turn it into a closed one on saving.

module RoomsHelper
  def link_to_room(room, **attributes, &)
    link_to room_path(room), **attributes, data: {
      rooms_list_target: "room", room_id: room.id, badge_dot_target: "unread", sorted_list_target: "item"
    }.merge(attributes.delete(:data) || {}), &
  end

  def link_to_edit_room(room, &)
    link_to \
      [ :edit, @room ],
      class: "btn",
      style: "view-transition-name: edit-room-#{@room.id}",
      data: { room_id: @room.id },
      &
  end

  def link_back_to_last_room_visited
    if last_room = last_room_visited
      link_back_to room_path(last_room)
    else
      link_back_to root_path
    end
  end

  def button_to_delete_room(room, url: nil)
    button_to url || room_url(room), method: :delete, class: "btn btn--negative max-width", aria: { label: "Delete #{room.name}" },
        data: { turbo_confirm: "Are you sure you want to delete this room and all messages in it? This can’t be undone." } do
      image_tag("trash.svg", aria: { hidden: "true" }, size: 20) +
      tag.span(room_display_name(room), class: "overflow-ellipsis")
    end
  end

  def button_to_jump_to_newest_message
    tag.button \
        class: "message-area__return-to-latest btn",
        data: { action: "messages#returnToLatest", messages_target: "latest" },
        hidden: true do
      image_tag("arrow-down.svg", aria: { hidden: "true" }, size: 20) +
      tag.span("Jump to newest message", class: "for-screen-reader")
    end
  end

  def submit_room_button_tag
    button_tag class: "btn btn--reversed txt-large center", type: "submit" do
      image_tag("check.svg", aria: { hidden: "true" }, size: 20) +
      tag.span("Save", class: "for-screen-reader")
    end
  end

  def composer_form_tag(room, &)
    form_with model: Message.new, url: room_messages_path(room),
      id: "composer", class: "margin-block flex-item-grow contain", data: composer_data_options(room), &
  end

  def room_display_name(room, for_user: Current.user)
    if room.direct?
      room.users.without(for_user).pluck(:name).to_sentence.presence || for_user&.name
    else
      room.name
    end
  end

  private
    def composer_data_options(room)
      {
        controller: "composer drop-target",
        action: composer_data_actions,
        composer_messages_outlet: "#message-area",
        composer_toolbar_class: "composer--rich-text", composer_room_id_value: room.id
      }
    end

    def composer_data_actions
      drag_and_drop_actions = "drop-target:drop@window->composer#dropFiles"

      trix_attachment_actions =
        "trix-file-accept->composer#preventAttachment refresh-room:online@window->composer#online"

      remaining_actions =
        "typing-notifications#stop paste->composer#pasteFiles turbo:submit-end->composer#submitEnd refresh-room:offline@window->composer#offline"

      [ drop_target_actions, drag_and_drop_actions, trix_attachment_actions, remaining_actions ].join(" ")
    end
end

## Development

### Setting up

First, get everything installed and configured with:

```sh
bin/setup
```

This installs the system packages Campfire needs (SQLite, ffmpeg), the right Ruby version (via [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev)), and the app's gems; prepares the database; and starts Redis (in a Docker container called `campfire-redis`, if it isn't already running locally).

If you want to start over at any point, run:

```sh
bin/setup --reset
```

### Running the server

Start the development server with:

```sh
bin/dev
```

You'll be able to access the app at http://localhost:3000.

On first run you'll be guided through creating your admin account, and you can sign in with that account from then on.

Note that Campfire needs Redis (for Action Cable, caching, and background jobs), so if you've restarted your machine or stopped the container, `docker start campfire-redis` will bring it back.

### Web Push notifications

Campfire uses VAPID (Voluntary Application Server Identification) keys to send browser push notifications. For notifications to work in development you'll need to generate a key pair and set these environment variables:

- `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`

You can generate a fresh pair (along with a secret key base, which you can ignore in development) by running:

```sh
script/admin/generate-secrets
```

### Running tests

Run the unit tests with:

```sh
bin/rails test
```

And the browser-based system tests with:

```sh
bin/rails test:system
```

Before pushing your changes, you can run the full CI suite locally - style checks, security audits, and all the tests - with a single command:

```sh
bin/ci
```

### Contributing

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
If you'd like to contribute your changes back, please read our [contributing guide](../CONTRIBUTING.md) first.

## Development

### Setting up

First, get everything installed and configured with:

```sh
bin/setup
```

This installs the system packages Campfire needs (SQLite, ffmpeg), the right Ruby version (via [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev)), and the app's gems; prepares the database; and starts Redis (in a Docker container called `campfire-redis`, if it isn't already running locally).

If you want to start over at any point, run:

```sh
bin/setup --reset
```

### Running the server

Start the development server with:

```sh
bin/dev
```

You'll be able to access the app at http://localhost:3000.

On first run you'll be guided through creating your admin account, and you can sign in with that account from then on.

Note that Campfire needs Redis (for Action Cable, caching, and background jobs), so if you've restarted your machine or stopped the container, `docker start campfire-redis` will bring it back.

### Web Push notifications

Campfire uses VAPID (Voluntary Application Server Identification) keys to send browser push notifications. For notifications to work in development you'll need to generate a key pair and set these environment variables:

- `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`

You can generate a fresh pair (along with a secret key base, which you can ignore in development) by running:

```sh
script/admin/generate-secrets
```

### Running tests

Run the unit tests with:

```sh
bin/rails test
```

And the browser-based system tests with:

```sh
bin/rails test:system
```

Before pushing your changes, you can run the full CI suite locally - style checks, security audits, and all the tests - with a single command:

```sh
bin/ci
```

### Contributing

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
If you'd like to contribute your changes back, please read our [contributing guide](../CONTRIBUTING.md) first.

===
class ContentFilters::RemoveSoloUnfurledLinkText < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?
    normalize_tweet_url(solo_unfurled_url) == normalize_tweet_url(content.to_plain_text)
  end

  def apply
    fragment.replace("div") { |node| node.tap { |n| n.inner_html = unfurled_links.first.to_s } }
  end

  private
    TWITTER_DOMAINS = %w[ x.com twitter.com ]
    TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING = { "x.com" => "twitter.com" }

    def solo_unfurled_url
      unfurled_links.first["href"] if unfurled_links.size == 1
    end

    def unfurled_links
      fragment.find_all("action-text-attachment[@content-type='#{ActionText::Attachment::OpengraphEmbed::OPENGRAPH_EMBED_CONTENT_TYPE}']")
    end

    def normalize_tweet_url(url)
      return url unless twitter_url?(url)

      uri = URI.parse(url)

      uri.dup.tap do |u|
        u.host = TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING[uri.host&.downcase] || uri.host
        u.query = nil
      end.to_s
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      url
    end

    def twitter_url?(url)
      url.present? && TWITTER_DOMAINS.any? { |domain| url.strip.include?(domain) }
    end
end
class ContentFilters::SanitizeAttributes < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?

    TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING = { "x.com" => "twitter.com" }

    def normalize_tweet_url(url)
      return url unless twitter_url?(url)

      uri = URI.parse(url)

      uri.dup.tap do |u|

        u.query = nil
      end.to_s
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      url
    end

    def twitter_url?(url)
      url.present? && TWITTER_DOMAINS.any? { |domain| url.strip.include?(domain) }
    end

module Rack
  class MethodOverride
    HTTP_METHODS = %w[GET HEAD PUT POST DELETE OPTIONS PATCH LINK UNLINK]

    METHOD_OVERRIDE_PARAM_KEY = "_method"
    HTTP_METHOD_OVERRIDE_HEADER = "HTTP_X_HTTP_METHOD_OVERRIDE"
    ALLOWED_METHODS = %w[POST]

    def initialize(app)
      @app = app
    end

    def call(env)

        method = method_override(env)
        if HTTP_METHODS.include?(method)
          env[RACK_METHODOVERRIDE_ORIGINAL_METHOD] = env[REQUEST_METHOD]
          env[REQUEST_METHOD] = method

- **Data model:** a separate `bots` table (`user_id` → a real `User` row, `creator_id`, unique `bot_key`). Bots are real users, so existing membership, mention, message, and push code works unchanged. The credential stays out of `users`.

- **Management:** `/bots` (index, new, edit, delete), scoped to the creator or admins.
- **Sensitive credential:** shown only to its creator and admins, `no-store` caching, masked in request logs and Sentry, and bots excluded from the people list.

module TurboTestHelper
  def assert_rendered_turbo_stream_broadcast(*streambles, action:, target:, &block)
    streams = find_broadcasts_for(*streambles)
    target = ActionView::RecordIdentifier.dom_id(*target)
    assert_select Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(streams), %(turbo-stream[action="#{action}"][target="#{target}"]), &block
  end

  private
    def find_broadcasts_for(*streambles)
      broadcasting = streambles.collect do |streamble|
        streamble.try(:to_gid_param) || streamble
      end.join(":")

      broadcasts = ActionCable.server.pubsub.broadcasts(broadcasting)
      broadcasts.collect { |b| JSON.parse(b) }.join("\n\n")
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class BotsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in :david
    @bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:david))
  end

  test "index lists the bots you created with their name and bot code" do
    get bots_url

    assert_response :success
    assert_select "li#%s" % dom_id(@bot) do
      assert_select "strong", text: "Deploy Bot"
      assert_select "label[for=?]", dom_id(@bot, :bot_key), text: "Bot code"
      assert_select "input[id=?][readonly][value=?]", dom_id(@bot, :bot_key), @bot.bot_key
    end
  end

  test "index shows every bot on one page, without pagination" do
    12.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: users(:david)) }

    get bots_url

    assert_select "li.membership-item", count: 13
    assert_select ".pagination, .next-page, #next_page_container", count: 0
  end

  test "index doesn't list or expose bots created by someone else" do
    other = Bot.create!(name: "Someone Else's Bot", creator: users(:jz))

    get bots_url

    assert_select "strong", text: "Someone Else's Bot", count: 0
    assert_not_includes response.body, other.bot_key
  end

  test "administrators see every bot" do
    other = Bot.create!(name: "Someone Else's Bot", creator: users(:jz))
    sign_in :jz
    get bots_url
    assert_select "strong", text: "Someone Else's Bot", count: 1
    assert_not_includes response.body, @bot.bot_key

    sign_in :jason
    get bots_url
    assert_select "strong", text: "Deploy Bot"
    assert_select "strong", text: "Someone Else's Bot"
    assert_includes response.body, other.bot_key
  end

  test "index tells browsers and caches not to keep a copy of bot codes" do
    get bots_url

    assert_includes response.headers["Cache-Control"], "no-store"
  end

  test "index links to each bot's edit page by name" do
    get bots_url

    assert_select "a[href=?][aria-label=?]", edit_bot_path(@bot), "Edit Deploy Bot"
  end

  test "new" do
    get new_bot_url

    assert_response :success
    assert_select "form[action=?]", bots_path do
      assert_select "input[name=?][placeholder=?]", "bot[name]", "Name the bot"
      assert_select "input[name=?][type=file]", "bot[avatar]"
      assert_select "button", text: /Save changes/
    end
  end

  test "create makes a bot user that joins every open room and redirects to the list" do
    assert_difference -> { Bot.count }, +1 do
      assert_difference -> { User.count }, +1 do
        post bots_url, params: { bot: { name: "Deploy Bot 2" } }
      end
    end

    assert_redirected_to bots_url

    bot = Bot.last
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot 2", bot.name
    assert_equal users(:david), bot.creator
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.rooms.opens.count
  end

  test "create with an avatar attaches it to the bot" do
    post bots_url, params: { bot: { name: "Avatar Bot", avatar: fixture_file_upload("pixel.bmp", "image/bmp") } }

    assert Bot.last.user.avatar.attached?
  end

  test "create without a name is rejected and creates nothing" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Bot.count } do
      assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) do
        post bots_url, params: { bot: { name: "" } }
      end
    end
  end

  test "create doesn't leave the new bot's code in the flash or redirect" do
    post bots_url, params: { bot: { name: "Quiet Bot" } }

    assert_not_includes response.location.to_s, Bot.last.bot_key
    assert_nil flash[:notice]&.include?(Bot.last.bot_key) || nil
  end

  test "edit" do
    get edit_bot_url(@bot)

    assert_response :success
    assert_select "input[name=?][value=?]", "bot[name]", "Deploy Bot"
    assert_select "button", text: "Delete this chat bot"
  end

  test "edit doesn't show the bot code" do
    get edit_bot_url(@bot)

    assert_not_includes response.body, @bot.bot_key
  end

  test "update changes the name" do
    patch bot_url(@bot), params: { bot: { name: "Renamed Bot" } }

    assert_redirected_to bots_url
    assert_equal "Renamed Bot", @bot.reload.name
    assert_equal "Renamed Bot", @bot.user.reload.name
  end

  test "update without choosing an avatar keeps the existing one" do
    @bot.user.avatar.attach io: File.open(file_fixture("../fixtures/files/pixel.bmp")), filename: "pixel.bmp", content_type: "image/bmp"
    assert @bot.user.reload.avatar.attached?

    patch bot_url(@bot), params: { bot: { name: "Renamed Bot", avatar: "" } }

    sign_in :jason

    assert_equal "Renamed by admin", other.reload.name
  end

  test "bot management requires a signed in user" do
    sign_out_user

    assert_redirected_to new_session_url
  end

  test "the account settings page links to the bots page" do
    get edit_account_url

    assert_select "a[href=?] .for-screen-reader", bots_path, text: "Set up chat bots"
  end

  test "the account settings page links to the bots page for members too" do
    sign_in :kevin
    get edit_account_url

    assert_select "a[href=?]", bots_path
  end

messages.content: Everything is red for the expected reasons. Now the implementation, starting with the `Bot` model. It keeps the bot's name and avatar on a real `User`, builds that user with an unguessable password, and owns the credential.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/bot.rb <<'EOF'
# A bot is a user that a person set up to post messages over HTTP. Its name and avatar live on its user, so it
# shows up in rooms, mentions and messages exactly like a person. The bot key is the credential its API requests
# are authenticated with: it's only shown to the bot's creator and administrators, and never written to logs.
class Bot < ApplicationRecord
  has_secure_token :bot_key

  belongs_to :user, autosave: true
  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validates :name, presence: true

  scope :ordered, -> { joins(:user).order("LOWER(users.name)") }
  scope :active, -> { joins(:user).merge(User.active) }
  scope :created_by, ->(user) { where(creator: user) }

  # Bot keys travel in the path of the message endpoint, so anything that records request paths (logs, error
  # reports) runs them through here to mask the key.
  def self.filter_path(path)
    path.sub(%r{(/rooms/[^/?]+/)[^/?]+(/messages)(?=\?|\z)}, '\1[FILTERED]\2')
  end

  def name
    user&.name
  end

  def name=(name)
    bot_user.name = name
  end

  def avatar=(avatar)
    bot_user.avatar = avatar
  end

  # Removing a bot keeps its messages, just as deactivating a person does, but its user stops being a member
  # of anything and its bot key stops working.
  def deactivate
    transaction do
      user.deactivate
      destroy!
    end
  end

  private
    # A bot never signs in, so nobody gets to know its password. The password digest column is required,
    # so the bot's user gets a random one that's thrown away.
    def bot_user
      user || build_user(password: SecureRandom.base58(64))
    end
end
EOF

messages.content: Rails' own query filtering works through a parameter filter that the app places in each request's environment, and a bare `env_for` request doesn't have it. So the test is wrong, not the patch. I'll build the test request from the app's env config, which is what a real request carries, and fix the model test's upload helper.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > test/lib/rails_ext/filtered_bot_path_test.rb <<'EOF'
require "test_helper"

class FilteredBotPathTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "the bot key is masked in the logged path of a bot message" do
    request = request_for "/rooms/42/aBcD1234eFgH5678iJkL9012/messages"

    assert_equal "/rooms/42/[FILTERED]/messages", request.filtered_path
  end

  test "the query string is still filtered as usual" do
    request = request_for "/rooms/42/aBcD1234eFgH5678iJkL9012/messages?token=abc"

    assert_equal "/rooms/42/[FILTERED]/messages?token=[FILTERED]", request.filtered_path
  end

  test "other paths are logged as they are" do
    assert_equal "/rooms/42/messages", request_for("/rooms/42/messages").filtered_path
    assert_equal "/rooms/42/refresh", request_for("/rooms/42/refresh").filtered_path
    assert_equal "/bots/7/edit", request_for("/bots/7/edit").filtered_path
  end

  test "full URLs in error reports are masked too" do
    assert_equal "https://chat.example.com/rooms/42/[FILTERED]/messages",
      Bot.filter_path("https://chat.example.com/rooms/42/aBcD1234eFgH5678iJkL9012/messages")
  end

  private
    # A request as the app sees it, with the app's parameter filter in its environment
    def request_for(path)
      env = Rack::MockRequest.env_for(path, method: "POST").merge(Rails.application.env_config)

      ActionDispatch::Request.new(env)
    end
end
EOF

messages.content: That settles it: this is Rails' per-form CSRF protection working as designed. arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > docs/bots.md <<'EOF'
# Chat bots

Bots are members of rooms that post messages over HTTP. A bot is set up by a chat member and then driven
by a shell script or CI job, which authenticates with the bot's code.

## Setting up a bot (people)

1. Open account settings (`/account/edit`) and click the bot icon, "Set up chat bots" (`/bots`).
2. "Add a chat bot" opens `/bots/new`. The bot name is required, the avatar is optional. "Save changes" creates
   the bot and returns to `/bots`.
3. Each bot on the list shows its name and its **bot code** in a read-only "Bot code" field. Copy it into your
   script or CI secrets. Treat it like a password.
4. "Edit <name>" changes the name and avatar. "Delete this chat bot" (with a confirmation) removes the bot.

Who sees and manages what:

- Any chat member can create bots. A member sees, edits and deletes only the bots they created.
- Administrators see and manage every bot.
- The bots page lists all of them on one page (no pagination).
- Bots are left out of the people list on the account page, since they're managed from `/bots`.

Bots join all open rooms, like any new person. They can be added to closed rooms the same way people are
(the access switches in the room's settings).

## Posting messages (bots)

The raw request body is the message. There is no JSON envelope and there are no field names:

```sh
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

| Response | When |
| --- | --- |
| `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:message_id` | The message was posted. |
| `422 Unprocessable Content` | The body is empty or only whitespace, or it isn't valid UTF-8. |
| `404 Not Found` | The room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it. |
| `401 Unauthorized` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bot realm="Campfire"`) | The bot code is unknown, the bot was deleted, or its user was deactivated or banned. |

Details:

- The body is text, whatever `Content-Type` the client sends. `curl -d` sends form encoding by default, and
  that doesn't change the message: `Disk at 100% done` is posted as written.
- Line breaks are kept. Markup is shown as text, so `<b>` in a message appears literally.
- Attachments aren't supported. The body is the whole message.
- The message shows the bot's name as its author. It's broadcast to the room, updates unread markers, and
  triggers push notifications exactly like a person's message.
- `Location` is `/messages/:id`, as specified. Messages are room-scoped in this app, so that URL returns 404
  today. A future change could resolve it to the room's message.

## Design notes

**Data model.** A bot is a `bots` row (`user_id`, `creator_id`, `bot_key`) that points at an ordinary `users`
row. The user holds the bot's name, avatar and room memberships, so everything that handles people (membership,
mentions, messages, push, avatars) works for bots without changes. The credential lives only in `bots`, so it
never appears when users are serialized or listed.

**Bot users can't sign in.** The `users.password_digest` column is `NOT NULL`, so a bot's user gets a random
password that nobody learns. A bot has no email address, and its profile doesn't offer the auto-login link.

**Deleting a bot** deactivates its user, the same way removing a person does: the user leaves every room (direct
rooms excepted), and its messages stay. The `bots` row is destroyed, which kills the bot code. Deactivated and
banned users fail authentication too (`Bot.active`).

**Posting.** `Bots::MessagesController` is unauthenticated by session and doesn't check CSRF tokens, because
the bot code in the path is the credential. Rails parses form bodies before any action runs, and it rejects
text such as `100% done` with a 400. The controller therefore declares the body as not being form fields
(`process_action`). `Bots::MessagesControllerTest` covers this.

**Authorization.** Editing and deleting use `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)`, which means administrator or
creator, the same rule used for other records here.

## Protecting bot codes

A bot code grants the ability to post as the bot, so:

- It's shown only on `/bots`, to the bot's creator and administrators. The edit page doesn't show it.
- `/bots` is served with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `turbo-cache-control: no-cache`, so neither the browser nor
  Turbo's page cache keeps a copy.
- It never appears in messages, broadcasts, redirects, flash messages or JSON.
- Rails' parameter filter masks it (`bot_key` matches the existing `_key` filter), so `Parameters:` log lines show
  `[FILTERED]`.
- Rails masks only the query string when it logs a path, so `lib/rails_ext/filtered_bot_path.rb` masks the code in
  the path too: `Started POST "/rooms/1/[FILTERED]/messages"`. `Bot.filter_path` does the same for Sentry request
  URLs (`config/initializers/sentry.rb`).
- The code is generated by `has_secure_token` (24 base58 characters, about 140 bits) and is unique in the database.

Known limits:

- The code is stored in plain text, because the page has to show it again. Anyone with database access can read it.
- ActiveRecord's SQL debug logging prints the value in the `bots.bot_key` query, in development or with
  `RAILS_LOG_LEVEL=debug`. Session tokens already appear the same way. Production logs at `info` by default.
- Reverse-proxy access logs record the full path, which includes the code. Treat those logs as sensitive.

Not built yet: rotating a bot code (`regenerate_bot_key` is available), rate limiting failed code attempts, and
per-bot scopes.

## Code map

- `app/models/bot.rb` (credential, creator, name/avatar delegated to the user, `deactivate`)
- `app/models/user.rb` (`has_one :bot`, `bot?`, `without_bots`)
- `app/controllers/bots_controller.rb` (`/bots` management pages)
- `app/controllers/bots/messages_controller.rb` (the posting API)
- `app/views/bots/` (list, form, new, edit)
- `lib/rails_ext/filtered_bot_path.rb` (log masking)
- `db/migrate/*_create_bots.rb`

Tests: `test/models/bot_test.rb`, `test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb`,
`test/controllers/bots/messages_controller_test.rb`, `test/lib/rails_ext/filtered_bot_path_test.rb`, plus
bot cases in the accounts, users and closed-room controller tests.
EOF

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Chat bots

Bots are members of rooms that post messages over HTTP. A bot is set up by a chat member and then driven
by a shell script or CI job, which authenticates with the bot's code.

## Setting up a bot (people)

1. Open account settings (`/account/edit`) and click the bot icon, "Set up chat bots" (`/bots`).
2. "Add a chat bot" opens `/bots/new`. The bot name is required, the avatar is optional. "Save changes" creates
   the bot and returns to `/bots`.
3. Each bot on the list shows its name and its **bot code** in a read-only "Bot code" field. Copy it into your
   script or CI secrets. Treat it like a password.
4. "Edit <name>" changes the name and avatar. "Delete this chat bot" (with a confirmation) removes the bot.

Who sees and manages what:

- Any chat member can create bots. A member sees, edits and deletes only the bots they created.
- Administrators see and manage every bot.
- The bots page lists all of them on one page (no pagination).
- Bots are left out of the people list on the account page, since they're managed from `/bots`.

Bots join all open rooms, like any new person. They can be added to closed rooms the same way people are
(the access switches in the room's settings).

## Posting messages (bots)

The raw request body is the message. There is no JSON envelope and there are no field names:

```sh
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

| Response | When |
| --- | --- |
| `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:message_id` | The message was posted. |
| `422 Unprocessable Content` | The body is empty or only whitespace, or it isn't valid UTF-8. |
| `404 Not Found` | The room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it. |
| `401 Unauthorized` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bot realm="Campfire"`) | The bot code is unknown, the bot was deleted, or its user was deactivated or banned. |

Details:

- The body is text, whatever `Content-Type` the client sends. `curl -d` sends form encoding by default, and
  that doesn't change the message: `Disk at 100% done` is posted as written.
- Line breaks are kept. Markup is shown as text, so `<b>` in a message appears literally.
- Attachments aren't supported. The body is the whole message.
- The message shows the bot's name as its author. It's broadcast to the room, updates unread markers, and
  triggers push notifications exactly like a person's message.
- `Location` is `/messages/:id`, as specified. Messages are room-scoped in this app, so that URL returns 404
  today. A future change could resolve it to the room's message.

## Design notes

**Data model.** A bot is a `bots` row (`user_id`, `creator_id`, `bot_key`) that points at an ordinary `users`
row. The user holds the bot's name, avatar and room memberships, so everything that handles people (membership,
mentions, messages, push, avatars) works for bots without changes. The credential lives only in `bots`, so it
never appears when users are serialized or listed.

**Bot users can't sign in.** The `users.password_digest` column is `NOT NULL`, so a bot's user gets a random
password that nobody learns. A bot has no email address, and its profile doesn't offer the auto-login link.
"
